title: A1 real-world mission
goal: Get through your first week in Montréal in French: find your apartment, order at a café, take the bus and book an appointment, then see what comes next in A2.

example.fr: La clé est chez la voisine.
example.en: The key is at the neighbour's.
My neighbour's name is Mrs. Lavoie.

items.en: What can I get you? (a server speaking)
I'd like to make an appointment.

blocks.title: The mission
blocks.body:
You have just landed in Montréal. Over four days you need to:

- **Day 1:** find your new apartment and get the key
- **Day 2:** order breakfast at a café
- **Day 3:** take the bus downtown
- **Day 4:** call a clinic to book an appointment

Each day mixes **reading, listening and writing**, exactly as in real life: you read a message, hear someone answer, then say or write what you need. There are 12 graded items. Aim for **80%** to pass the final A1 checkpoint. After the graded part, you write one message and make one phone call yourself.
Treat it as the real thing: read the documents once carefully, play each recording no more than twice, and write your answers without looking anything up.

steps.title: Days 1 and 2: The apartment and the café
steps.intro: Your landlord has sent you a message. Read it, then find your way.

blocks.title: A message from your landlord
blocks.fr:
Bonjour et bienvenue à Montréal !
L'appartement est au 4520, rue Fabre, appartement 3.
La clé est chez la voisine, madame Lavoie, à l'appartement 1. Elle est à la maison après 16 h.
Le métro Laurier est à dix minutes à pied.
Bonne installation !
Marc Gagnon

blocks.prompt: What is the address of your apartment?
options: 4520 Fabre Street, apartment 3
4520 Fabre Street, apartment 1
4250 Fabre Street, apartment 3
blocks.explain: [[au 4520, rue Fabre, appartement 3]]. Apartment 1 is Mrs. Lavoie's, the neighbour with the key.
optionFeedback: Apartment 1 is the neighbour's: [[madame Lavoie, à l'appartement 1]]. Yours is number 3.
Check the order of the digits: 4520.

blocks.prompt: Where do you get the key, and when?
options: From the neighbour, Mrs. Lavoie, after 4 p.m.
From Marc, at Laurier metro, after 4 p.m.
From the neighbour, Mrs. Lavoie, before 4 p.m.
blocks.explain: [[La clé est chez la voisine]] = the key is at the neighbour's place, and [[elle est à la maison après 16 h]] = she is home after 4 p.m. The metro is only mentioned to help you find the street.

blocks.fr: La rue Fabre ? Ce n'est pas loin. Allez tout droit, puis tournez à gauche dans la rue Rachel. C'est à cinq minutes.
blocks.en: Fabre Street? It's not far. Go straight ahead, then turn left onto Rachel Street. It's five minutes away.
blocks.prompt: You ask a passer-by the way to Fabre Street. How do you get there?
options: Go straight, then turn left onto Rachel Street
Go straight, then turn right onto Rachel Street
Turn left, then go straight for ten minutes
blocks.explain: [[Allez tout droit]] = go straight ahead; [[puis tournez à gauche]] = then turn left ([[à droite]] would be right). [[C'est à cinq minutes]]: five minutes, not ten.

blocks.fr: Bonjour ! Qu'est-ce que je vous sers ?
blocks.en: Hello! What can I get you?
blocks.prompt: Day 2: you are at the café counter. Choose the best reply.
options: Un café au lait, s'il vous plaît.
Je suis serveur, merci.
Oui, je vais bien.
blocks.explain: [[Qu'est-ce que je vous sers ?]] = What can I get you? You answer with what you want + [[s'il vous plaît]].

blocks.text: Je ___ aussi un croissant, s'il vous plaît.
blocks.en: I'd also like a croissant, please.
blocks.explain: [[Je voudrais]] is the polite way to order (I would like). [[Je vais]] needs an infinitive after it: [[je vais prendre]].

blocks.fr: Pour ici ? D'accord. Alors, un café au lait et un croissant, ça fait quatre dollars soixante-quinze.
blocks.en: For here? OK. So, a café au lait and a croissant, that comes to four dollars seventy-five.
blocks.prompt: The cashier tells you the price. How much do you pay?
blocks.explain: [[soixante-quinze]] = sixty + fifteen = 75, so $4.75 (written 4,75 $ in Québec). 65 would be [[soixante-cinq]].

steps.title: Days 3 and 4: The bus and the clinic
steps.intro: Today you go downtown, then you call a clinic.

blocks.title: A sign at the bus stop
blocks.fr:
Arrêt : Fabre / Laurier
Ligne 27 — Direction Centre-ville
Tous les jours, de 6 h à minuit
Un bus toutes les 15 minutes
Tarif : 3,75 $

blocks.prompt: It is 11:30 p.m. Is there still a bus downtown?
options: Yes, buses run until midnight.
No, the last bus is at 11 p.m.
No, buses only run during the day.
blocks.explain: [[Tous les jours, de 6 h à minuit]] = every day, from 6 a.m. to midnight. 11:30 p.m. is before midnight.

blocks.prompt: How often does the bus come?
options: Every 15 minutes
Every 50 minutes
Every hour
blocks.explain: [[Un bus toutes les 15 minutes]] = a bus every 15 minutes. It works like [[toutes les semaines]] (every week). Careful when you hear it: [[quinze]] (15) and [[cinquante]] (50) are easy to confuse.

blocks.prompt: Excuse me, which bus goes downtown? (formal)
accept: Excusez-moi, quel bus va au centre-ville ?
Excusez-moi, quel autobus va au centre-ville ?
Pardon, quel bus va au centre-ville ?
Pardon, quel autobus va au centre-ville ?
Excusez-moi, c'est quel bus pour le centre-ville ?
Excusez-moi, c'est quel autobus pour le centre-ville ?
Excusez-moi, c'est quel bus pour aller au centre-ville ?
Excusez-moi, c'est quel autobus pour aller au centre-ville ?
Excusez-moi, quel est le bus pour le centre-ville ?
blocks.explain: [[Quel]] agrees with [[bus]] (masculine). [[Aller au centre-ville]] = à + le centre-ville. In Québec you also hear [[l'autobus]].

blocks.fr: Clinique du Plateau, bonjour ! Un rendez-vous avec le docteur Roy ? Alors, j'ai une place mardi à neuf heures quinze ou mercredi à quinze heures.
blocks.en: Plateau Clinic, hello! An appointment with Dr. Roy? So, I have a spot on Tuesday at 9:15 or Wednesday at 3 p.m.
blocks.prompt: Day 4: you call the clinic. Which times does the receptionist offer?
options: Tuesday at 9:15 a.m. or Wednesday at 3 p.m.
Tuesday at 9:15 a.m. or Wednesday at 5 p.m.
Thursday at 9:15 a.m. or Wednesday at 3 p.m.
blocks.explain: [[mardi à neuf heures quinze]] = Tuesday at 9:15; [[mercredi à quinze heures]] = Wednesday at 15 h, 3 p.m. Note that [[quinze]] appears twice: 9:15 and 15 h.

blocks.prompt: I'd like to make an appointment, please.
accept: Je voudrais prendre rendez-vous, s'il vous plaît.
S'il vous plaît, je voudrais prendre rendez-vous.
blocks.explain: “To make an appointment” is [[prendre rendez-vous]] in French, with no article. [[Faire]] is the English trap.
[[Pouvoir]] + infinitive: [[je peux venir]]. Days take no preposition: [[mardi matin]] = on Tuesday morning.

steps.title: Your turn: write and call
steps.intro: Two last missions. Use the checklist, then compare with the **A1 model** and the **Strong A1 model**.

blocks.prompt: Write a message to a friend back home about your new life in Montréal (35–60 words). Say where you live, what there is in your neighbourhood, one thing you like or don't like, and one thing you are going to do soon. Use the present and aller + infinitive.
blocks.promptFr: Écrivez un message à un ami ou à une amie : votre nouvelle vie à Montréal.
checklist: A greeting with tu: Salut + name !
Where you live: J'habite dans… / rue…
Your neighbourhood: Dans mon quartier, il y a…
A like or dislike with a reason: J'aime… mais… / Je n'aime pas…
A plan with aller + infinitive: Samedi, je vais…
A friendly closing: Bises, / À bientôt ! + your name
Final check: agreement, accents, ne… pas

models.label: A1 model
models.fr: Salut Nadia ! Je suis à Montréal maintenant. J'habite dans un petit appartement, rue Fabre. Dans mon quartier, il y a un parc, des cafés et une épicerie. J'aime beaucoup le quartier, mais il fait froid ! La semaine prochaine, je vais commencer mon cours de français. Bises, Amira
models.en: Hi Nadia! I'm in Montréal now. I live in a small apartment on Fabre Street. In my neighbourhood, there's a park, some cafés and a grocery store. I really like the neighbourhood, but it's cold! Next week, I'm going to start my French class. Love, Amira

models.label: Strong A1 model
models.fr: Salut Nadia ! Bonjour de Montréal ! J'habite dans un 3 ½ sur le Plateau, près du métro Laurier. Mon quartier est super : il y a des cafés, un grand parc et beaucoup de petits magasins. Les gens sont gentils, mais il fait déjà froid et je n'ai pas de manteau ! Alors, samedi, je vais magasiner. Je t'embrasse, Raj
models.en: Hi Nadia! Hello from Montréal! I live in a 3 ½ in the Plateau, near Laurier metro. My neighbourhood is great: there are cafés, a big park and lots of little shops. People are nice, but it's already cold and I don't have a coat! So on Saturday I'm going shopping (“magasiner” is Québec French; in France, “faire les magasins”). Big hug, Raj

blocks.prompt: Call the Clinique du Plateau (45 seconds). Greet the receptionist, give and spell your name, ask for an appointment, say when you are available (and when you are not), ask what you need to bring, and thank them. Imagine the answers.
blocks.promptFr: Vous téléphonez à la clinique pour prendre rendez-vous.
checklist: Polite greeting with vous: Bonjour, madame / monsieur
Your name, spelled: Je m'appelle…, ça s'écrit…
The request: Je voudrais prendre rendez-vous, s'il vous plaît.
When you can come: Je peux venir mardi matin.
When you can't, with a reason: Mercredi, je ne peux pas : je travaille.
A question: Qu'est-ce que je dois apporter ?
If needed: Vous pouvez répéter, s'il vous plaît ?
Thanks and closing: Merci beaucoup, à mardi !

models.label: A1 model
models.fr: Bonjour, madame. Je m'appelle Sofia Reyes. Reyes, ça s'écrit R-E-Y-E-S. Je voudrais prendre rendez-vous avec un médecin, s'il vous plaît. … Mardi à neuf heures quinze ? Oui, je peux venir mardi matin. Mercredi, je ne peux pas. Qu'est-ce que je dois apporter ? … D'accord. Merci beaucoup, bonne journée !
models.en: Hello, madam. My name is Sofia Reyes. Reyes is spelled R-E-Y-E-S. I'd like to make an appointment with a doctor, please. … Tuesday at 9:15? Yes, I can come on Tuesday morning. I can't come on Wednesday. What do I need to bring? … OK. Thank you very much, have a good day! (The … mark the receptionist's answers.)

models.label: Strong A1 model
models.fr: Bonjour, madame ! Je m'appelle Alex Martin, M-A-R-T-I-N. Je suis nouveau à Montréal et je voudrais prendre rendez-vous avec le docteur Roy, s'il vous plaît. … Pardon, vous pouvez répéter plus lentement ? … Mardi à neuf heures quinze ou mercredi à quinze heures ? Mercredi, je ne peux pas : je travaille l'après-midi. Je préfère mardi matin. Qu'est-ce que je dois apporter ? … Ma carte d'assurance maladie, d'accord. Merci beaucoup, à mardi !
models.en: Hello, madam! My name is Alex Martin, M-A-R-T-I-N. I'm new in Montréal and I'd like to make an appointment with Dr. Roy, please. … Sorry, can you repeat that more slowly? … Tuesday at 9:15 or Wednesday at 3 p.m.? I can't do Wednesday: I work in the afternoon. I prefer Tuesday morning. What do I need to bring? … My health insurance card, OK. Thank you very much, see you on Tuesday! (The … mark the receptionist's answers.)

steps.title: You did it: A1 is complete

blocks.title: What A1 means
blocks.body:
Finishing A1 means you can handle **simple, everyday exchanges** when the other person speaks slowly and is ready to help. Concretely, you can now:

- introduce yourself and others, and answer questions about where you live, your family, your work and what you like
- understand signs, short messages, timetables and simple ads
- catch numbers, prices, times and places in short announcements and voicemails
- write a short note, fill in a form, and accept or refuse an invitation
- ask for information, order in a café, ask for directions and book an appointment

All of this with the **present tense**, **aller + infinitive** for plans, and the core of A1 grammar: être and avoir, articles, agreement, negation and questions. That is a real foundation: everything in A2 is built on it.

blocks.title: What comes next in A2
blocks.body:
A2 takes you from *now* to **before and later**, and from simple exchanges to **everyday situations you manage on your own**:

- **The passé composé**, to say what you did: [[J'ai visité Québec.]] [[Je suis allée au marché.]]
- **The imparfait**, to describe the past and old habits: [[Quand j'étais petit, j'habitais à Tunis.]]
- **The futur simple**, for plans and promises: [[L'année prochaine, je travaillerai à Ottawa.]]
- **Pronouns** that make you sound natural: [[je le prends]], [[je lui téléphone]], [[j'y vais]]
- **Real situations**: buying tickets, explaining a health problem, solving a problem with your apartment, comparing and returning items, writing practical emails

The first A2 unit starts with the question everyone hears on Monday morning: [[Qu'est-ce que tu as fait en fin de semaine ?]] (What did you do on the weekend? [[Fin de semaine]] is the Québec word; in France, [[le week-end]].)

blocks.title: A1 and your Canadian goals
blocks.body: A1 is the foundation, not yet an exam target. For Canadian citizenship, applicants aged 18 to 54 must currently show **CLB / NCLC level 4** in **speaking and listening**, in English or French. CLB/NCLC is a Canadian scale, not the CEFR (A1, A2, B1…): the two do not match exactly, but level 4 is generally a little above what this A1 course covers. Immigration programs such as Express Entry usually ask for higher levels. Rules and accepted tests change, so always check the official IRCC website. The A2 and B1 levels of this course are built with TEF Canada and TCF Canada in mind, so keep going.

summary:
- **Bravo ! You have finished A1**, the foundation level of French.
- You can get through a first week in a French-speaking city: read an address and a timetable, follow directions, order at a café and book an appointment
- You can introduce yourself, describe your home and write short, useful messages
- Next stop: **A2**, where you start talking about the past and the future. [[On continue !]]
